result.summary: Restricts libbitcoinkernel to allow only one active logging connection per process at a time. Renames the entry point to btck_global_logging_connection_create, fails subsequent concurrent connection attempts, and replaces the global btck_logging_set_min_level with a handle-specific btck_logging_connection_set_min_level defaulting to Info on creation.
result.problem: The underlying KernelLogger is a process-wide singleton, so all connections share the same log stream and minimum log level. Exposing an API that allowed creating multiple btck_LoggingConnection handles gave consumers the false impression that independent loggers could be instantiated.
evidence: Description notes: 'Kernel logging is inherently global: KernelLogger is a process-wide singleton, so every connection receives every log entry and shares the minimum level. Multiple btck_LoggingConnection handles give the false impression of independent loggers.'
result.scope_notes: Modifies the experimental libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper.
result.changed_since_previous: The core approach and interface changes remain unchanged.
result.card: Restricts libbitcoinkernel to allow only one active logging connection per process at a time. Because the underlying kernel logger is a process-wide singleton, permitting multiple connections gave library consumers the false impression that independent loggers could be configured. Attempting to create a second connection now fails, the constructor is renamed to btck_global_logging_connection_create, and log level configuration is moved to the connection handle.

risk.why: A mistake could break logging initialization or callback delivery for consumers of libbitcoinkernel.
